blocks.text: Setting up your SEO workspace on Mac

Start by organizing your workspace to separate client work from internal tasks. Use the sidebar to group workspaces by client. If you have many clients, create a master dashboard page. This page acts as your home base. Use a database to list all active projects. You can filter this database by status or priority.

items: Create a new page for each client.
Add a database for content calendars.
Use a separate database for technical audit logs.
Keep a master task list with dates and owners.

blocks.text: Technical audits require detail. Use a database property to track the status of each issue found during a crawl. You can use statuses like To Do, In Progress, and Fixed. Add a multi-select property for issue types such as broken links, missing meta descriptions, or slow load times. This makes it easy to filter by category when you talk to developers.
Use the /callout command to highlight critical audit items. This draws attention to urgent tasks that need immediate developer action.
blocks.title: Highlight urgent issues

blocks.text: When you are deep in a crawl report, you do not want to hunt for menu items. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur where a setting is. Lazur can point at the filter button in your database. This saves you from clicking through submenus. If you are stuck on a formula for your keyword tracker, ask Lazur to explain how to write it. You can also use Lazur to dictate notes while you review a site. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on the data.

Many SEO specialists struggle with tab fatigue. Keep your research in your browser but move your final strategy docs to Notion. Use the /embed command to bring in live data from Google Sheets. This way, your reports stay updated without manual copy and paste. If you need to share a report, use the Share menu to invite clients as guests. You can lock specific pages so they cannot edit your core strategy.

Do not overcomplicate your database structure early on. Start with simple properties. You can add more later as your process evolves. Another mistake is forgetting to use templates. Create a template for your monthly SEO reports. This ensures you include all necessary metrics every time. Use the ⌘ P shortcut to search your workspace instead of clicking through folders. This is the fastest way to move between client pages.

Review your current workflow. Identify one part of your process that feels slow. Is it reporting? Is it task tracking? Set up a dedicated page in Notion for that specific area. Test it for one week. If it saves you time, expand it to other clients. Remember that your workspace should serve your process, not the other way around.

faq.question: Can I use Notion for technical SEO audits?
faq.answer: Yes, Notion is ideal for tracking audit progress. Use databases to manage issue status, priority, and assigned developers.

faq.question: How do I find Notion shortcuts on Mac?
faq.answer: Press Shift + ? on your keyboard to see the full list of available shortcuts in the Notion app.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside the Notion app?
faq.answer: Lazur works on your entire screen. You can ask it to point at buttons, explain features, or guide you through settings in Notion.

faq.question: What is the best way to manage multiple client projects?
faq.answer: Use a master dashboard page with a linked database. Filter the database by client property to see only the relevant tasks for one project.
